sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是本杰明·普林，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代，当我还在夜店打碟的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍爱的藏品去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个充满生机的、展示50年前美丽艺术品的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Bilboro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·比尔伯罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是“每日新闻”。

sentences.en: A few days ago, when Microsoft released a new version of its search engine, it claimed that it would reinvent how billions of people search the internet.
sentences.zh: 几天前，微软发布了其搜索引擎的新版本，并声称它将重塑数十亿人搜索互联网的方式。

sentences.en: Today, Kevin Roos, a tech columnist and co-host of the Times podcast Hard Fork, on whether that bold claim might actually be true.
sentences.zh: 今天，科技专栏作家、《时报》播客《硬分叉》联合主持人凯文·罗斯将探讨这一大胆的说法是否会成为现实。

sentences.en: Wednesday, February 15th.
sentences.zh: 2月15日，星期三。

sentences.en: Kevin, your judgment, as far as I am concerned, is pretty unerring when it comes to technology.
sentences.zh: 凯文，就我而言，你在科技方面的判断几乎是无可挑剔的。

sentences.en: But a couple of days ago, when you claimed that there was a big breakthrough in how we use artificial intelligence online, I was very skeptical.
sentences.zh: 但几天前，当你声称我们在网上使用人工智能的方式有了重大突破时，我非常怀疑。

sentences.en: And I was skeptical because you had just been on the show two months ago saying, lo and behold, there has been a big breakthrough in how we use artificial intelligence online.
sentences.zh: 我之所以怀疑，是因为两个月前你才刚上过节目，当时你说，看哪，我们在网上使用人工智能的方式有了重大突破。

sentences.en: So that's a lot of breakthroughs, maybe one too many.
sentences.zh: 所以那是相当多的突破，也许有点太多了。

sentences.en: So I'm going to ask you to make your case that something big has happened here.
sentences.zh: 因此，我请你证明这里确实发生了重大变化。

sentences.en: And please know that if it's not compelling, we don't have an episode.
sentences.zh: 请记住，如果不够引人注目，我们就不会做这期节目。

sentences.en: And we need an episode.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一期节目。

sentences.en: Well, I should say, I appreciate your confidence, but I am sort of like an advanced AI chatbot.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我得说，我很感激你的信任，但我有点像一个高级AI聊天机器人。

sentences.en: I can be occasionally helpful and correct, but also erratic.
sentences.zh: 我偶尔能帮上忙且言之有中，但也可能反复无常。

sentences.en: So, you know, take this all with a grain of salt.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，对这些话别太当真。

sentences.en: But I do believe we have an episode today because something very big and strange and I think important is happening in the world of internet search engines.
sentences.zh: 但我确实相信我们今天有一期节目，因为互联网搜索引擎的世界里正在发生一件非常重大、诡异且我认为很重要的事。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, tell that story.
sentences.zh: 那么，讲讲这个故事吧。

sentences.en: Make your argument.
sentences.zh: 说出你的论据。

sentences.en: So, a couple months ago, when we last spoke on the show, it was because this new AI tool had come out called ChatGPT.
sentences.zh: 所以，几个月前我们在节目中最后一次交谈时，是因为推出了一款名为ChatGPT的新AI工具。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which was this very user-friendly interface for this large language model developed by OpenAI.
sentences.zh: 它是OpenAI开发的大型语言模型的一个非常用户友好的界面。

sentences.en: And millions of people used it.
sentences.zh: 数以百万计的人都在使用它。

sentences.en: It became an overnight sensation.
sentences.zh: 它一夜之间成了轰动全球的现象。

sentences.en: But it did kind of feel for a little while like it was going to be a novelty.
sentences.zh: 但在短时间内，它确实让人觉得可能只是一时新鲜。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, in that episode, we treated it a little bit like a play thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在那期节目里，我们有点把它当成了一个玩具。

sentences.en: For those who missed our conversation, Kevin, you showed me how ChatGPT worked, how it can write stories, right?
sentences.zh: 对于错过我们对话的听众，凯文，你向我展示了ChatGPT是如何工作的，它如何能写故事，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, we wrote a story together, first in Shakespearean English, then in Mafioso prose.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们一起写了一个故事，先是用莎士比亚英语，然后是黑手党风格的散文。

sentences.en: This technology is incredibly creative and generative and it just kind of knocks your socks off.
sentences.zh: 这项技术具有令人难以置信的创造力和生成能力，简直让人惊叹不已。

sentences.en: But, you know, it felt like something that was kind of a party trick.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，它感觉就像是一个派对上的小把戏。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And a lot of people saw it that way.
sentences.zh: 很多人也是这么看的。

sentences.en: They, you know, played around with it and saw some cool things it could do.
sentences.zh: 他们，你知道的，拿它玩了玩，看到了它能做的一些酷炫的事情。

sentences.en: But maybe it didn't work its way into their daily routine.
sentences.zh: 但它可能并没有融入他们的日常生活。

sentences.en: But then, just a week or two ago, I got an email from Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 但就在一两周前，我收到了微软的一封电子邮件。

sentences.en: And Microsoft, not known for sort of thrilling announcements, I was a little skeptical.
sentences.zh: 微软向来不以激动人心的发布会著称，所以我有点怀疑。

sentences.en: But they were inviting me and a bunch of other reporters up to Seattle, to their campus in Redmond, Washington,
sentences.zh: 但他们邀请我和其他一帮记者去西雅图，去他们在华盛顿州雷德蒙德的园区，

sentences.en: to hear about a new announcement they were making related to artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 听取他们关于人工智能的新发布。

sentences.en: So, I went to the Microsoft campus, I sat down, I had a little moment of fear that it was going to turn out to be, like,
sentences.zh: 于是，我去了微软园区，坐了下来，心里闪过一丝恐惧，觉得这可能会变成，比如，

sentences.en: some boring update to their cloud services architecture that I would, like, regret my entire trip for.
sentences.zh: 对其云服务架构的一些无聊更新，让我会为这次旅行后悔莫及。

sentences.en: But it was more exciting than that.
sentences.zh: 但它比那更令人兴奋。

sentences.en: They revealed a new AI-powered version of Bing.
sentences.zh: 他们发布了由人工智能驱动的新版必应。

sentences.en: Bing, of course, being the also-ran backbencher of search engines.
sentences.zh: 当然，必应一直是搜索引擎里的落后追赶者和配角。

sentences.en: So, here I need to say that my skepticism has re-emerged.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里我得说，我的怀疑又卷土重来了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I don't blame you because Bing, for, you know, pretty much all of its existence, has been kind of a punchline in the tech world.
sentences.zh: 我不怪你，因为必应在其存在的几乎整个历史中，在科技界一直有点像个笑柄。

sentences.en: And it felt like being invited to the launch of a sequel for a movie that flopped the first time.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像是被邀请去参加一部第一部就扑街的电影的续集首映式。

sentences.en: Like, Bing, really, that's your big reveal?
sentences.zh: 就像是，必应，真的吗，这就是你的重大发布？

sentences.en: That's the thing that you were so excited about?
sentences.zh: 这就是让你如此兴奋的东西？

sentences.en: But it was.
sentences.zh: 但事实确实如此。

sentences.en: Well, explain that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，解释一下。

sentences.en: I mean, what exactly had they done with this relaunch?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们通过这次重新发布究竟做了什么？

sentences.en: And why did it seem to really matter?
sentences.zh: 为什么它看起来如此重要？

sentences.en: So, Microsoft, which has had a partnership with OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, announces that they are building OpenAI's software directly into Bing.
sentences.zh: 因此，与ChatGPT的创造者OpenAI建立合作伙伴关系的微软宣布，他们正在将OpenAI的软件直接内置到必应中。

sentences.en: They are basically taking this search engine and sort of frankensteining it together with this AI large language model built by OpenAI to make the new and relaunched Bing.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是将这个搜索引擎与OpenAI构建的AI大型语言模型“弗兰肯斯坦式”地拼凑在一起，打造出了全新且重新发布的必应。

sentences.en: Which might sound like kind of a boring product update, but it is actually a radical change.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能是一个无聊的产品更新，但它实际上是一个根本性的改变。

sentences.en: You know, search is the basic atomic unit of internet activity, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，搜索是互联网活动的基本原子单位，对吧？

sentences.en: When you go online to look something up or figure something out, the first thing you do is probably you Google it.
sentences.zh: 当你上网查阅某些东西或弄清楚某件事时，你做的第一件事可能就是用谷歌搜索一下。

sentences.en: That is, like, a very basic part of how billions of people use the internet.
sentences.zh: 这就像是数十亿人使用互联网的最基本的一部分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so a change to a search engine, even one as seemingly minor as Bing, that makes it work in a fundamentally different way is, I would argue, a pretty big deal.
sentences.zh: 因此，对搜索引擎的改变——即使是像必应这样看似微不足道的改变——只要能让它以根本不同的方式运作，我认为这就是一件相当大的事。

sentences.en: And what's so fundamentally different about an AI-driven search engine like Bing from the traditional way you and I Google all day long?
sentences.zh: 像必应这样的人工智能驱动的搜索引擎，与你我整天使用的传统谷歌搜索相比，到底有什么根本的不同？

sentences.en: So I think it could be helpful to just remind ourselves of what search has looked like for the past 20 plus years.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，回顾一下过去20多年来搜索是什么样子的，可能会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Educate us.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲吧。

sentences.en: So right now, when you search for something on Google, what you see is some ads, maybe some image results, a featured snippet with an attempt to answer whatever question you have.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，当你在谷歌上搜索某东西时，你看到的是一些广告，可能还有一些图片结果，以及一个试图回答你任何问题的精选摘要。

sentences.en: But the main event is that you get links, blue links to websites,
sentences.zh: 但重头戏是你得到了链接，指向网站的蓝色链接，

sentences.en: and those are the websites that Google believes are the most likely to contain the answer to whatever question you have.
sentences.zh: 这些就是谷歌认为最有可能包含你的任何问题答案的网站。

sentences.en: And so what Microsoft is trying to do using this OpenAI technology is to make a fundamentally different kind of search engine, one that doesn't just direct you to links,
sentences.zh: 因此，微软正试图利用这项OpenAI技术来打造一种根本不同类型的搜索引擎，它不仅仅是将你引导到链接，

sentences.en: but actually tries to use this AI to answer questions directly, to write you a custom answer for whatever you are looking for.
sentences.zh: 而是真正试图利用这种AI直接回答问题，为你所寻找的东西编写定制的答案。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: We've clearly reached the moment in our conversation where I need to see the friggin' thing to make sense of what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我们显然已经到了对话中的这个时刻：我需要亲眼看一看这个鬼东西，才能理解你在说什么。

sentences.en: Well, you can't see the thing directly because it's still invite-only.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你不能直接看到这个东西，因为它仍然是邀请制的。

sentences.en: You have to be sort of approved.
sentences.zh: 你得获得某种批准。

sentences.en: There's a wait liSt.
sentences.zh: 有一个候补名单。

sentences.en: Such a snob.
sentences.zh: 真是个势利眼。

sentences.en: I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: Well, take it up with Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 好吧，去找微软理论吧。

sentences.en: But I can do the next best thing, which is to share my screen with you so that you can see what this new Bing actually looks like.
sentences.zh: 但我可以做退而求其次的事，那就是把我的屏幕分享给你，这样你就能看到这个新必应到底长什么样。

sentences.en: So here's the new Bing.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是新必应。

sentences.en: Looks like a familiar search engine homepage.
sentences.zh: 看起来像一个熟悉的搜索引擎主页。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So you go to bing.com, and you can either use the traditional standard search box that comes up right in the center of the screen,
sentences.zh: 所以你访问bing.com，你可以使用屏幕正中央弹出的传统标准搜索框，

sentences.en: or up at the top, there's a little button that says chat.
sentences.zh: 或者在顶部，有一个写着“聊天”的小按钮。

sentences.en: And if you click on that, it opens this new interface, what it calls an AI-powered answer engine.
sentences.zh: 如果你点击它，就会打开这个新界面，也就是它所谓的AI驱动的答案引擎。

sentences.en: It says, welcome to the new Bing.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，欢迎来到新必应。

sentences.en: So let's try it out.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们来试试吧。

sentences.en: Today is Valentine's Day.
sentences.zh: 今天是情人节。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And so I am going to make my wife her favorite dish, French onion soup today.
sentences.zh: 所以我今天要给我妻子做她最喜欢的菜，法式洋葱汤。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But I need some side dishes to go with it.
sentences.zh: 但我需要一些配菜来搭配它。

sentences.en: So I'm going to go over to the chat tab here.
sentences.zh: 所以我要切换到这里的聊天标签页。

sentences.en: And now you can ask Bing anything.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以问必应任何问题。

sentences.en: And I'm going to say, I'm making a romantic Valentine's Day dinner for my wife.
sentences.zh: 我要说，我要为我的妻子准备一顿浪漫的情人节晚餐。

sentences.en: The main course is French onion soup.
sentences.zh: 主菜是法式洋葱汤。

sentences.en: And I need some side dishes to go with it.
sentences.zh: 我需要一些配菜来搭配。

sentences.en: She doesn't eat pork or shellfish.
sentences.zh: 她不吃猪肉或贝类。

sentences.en: What should I make?
sentences.zh: 我该做点什么？

sentences.en: It's a pretty long question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当长的问题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You've put this up.
sentences.zh: 你把这个发上去了。

sentences.en: It almost looks like a text exchange that you're having with Bing here.
sentences.zh: 它看起来几乎就像你正在和必应进行的一场文本交流。

sentences.en: And it's responding that it's searching for an answer.
sentences.zh: 它正在回应说它正在搜索答案。

sentences.en: It has some preamble.
sentences.zh: 它有一些前言。

sentences.en: It says, French onion soup is a delicious and hearty main course, but it can also be paired with some side dishes.
sentences.zh: 它说，法式洋葱汤是一道美味且顶饱的主菜，但它也可以搭配一些配菜。

sentences.en: So it's recommending, it says, one easy and tasty salad option is an arugula salad with cherry tomatoes, pine nuts, Parmesan cheese, and avocado.
sentences.zh: 所以它在推荐，它说，一个简单美味的沙拉选择是带有樱桃番茄、松子、帕玛森奶酪和牛油果的芝麻菜沙拉。

sentences.en: You can dress it with a simple lemon vinaigrette or olive oil and vinegar.
sentences.zh: 你可以用简单的柠檬油醋汁或橄榄油和醋来调味。

sentences.en: It's giving me one answer rather than a list of websites.
sentences.zh: 它给我的是一个答案，而不是一长串网站。

sentences.en: And there are small sort of annotations on the answer where if I wanted to, I could click through and go to these websites and look at some of the text on them.
sentences.zh: 答案上有一些小的注释，如果我想的话，我可以点击进去访问这些网站并查看其中的一些文本。

sentences.en: But this is just pulling out the recipe right here.
sentences.zh: 但这就是直接把食谱提取出来了。

sentences.en: And if that sounds good to me, which it actually does.
sentences.zh: 如果这听起来不错的话——事实上确实不错。

sentences.en: So now I'm going to say, write a shopping list for the arugula salad.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在要说，为芝麻菜沙拉写一份购物清单。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're just writing this right underneath this little essay you've been given about the salad.
sentences.zh: 你正好在这篇关于沙拉的小短文下面写下这些。

sentences.en: Sorted by Aisle.
sentences.zh: 按货架分类。

sentences.en: Of the grocery store.
sentences.zh: 杂货店的货架。

sentences.en: With amounts needed to make enough for two people.
sentences.zh: 附带做两人份所需的份量。

sentences.en: Okay, so it gave me the recipe now adjusted to make enough just for two people.
sentences.zh: 好的，现在它给我的食谱已经调整为刚好够两个人吃了。

sentences.en: So here's my shopping list now.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我的购物清单。

sentences.en: It says produce aisle, arugula leaves, cherry tomatoes, avocado, cheese and butter aisle, Parmesan cheese.
sentences.zh: 它说生鲜区，芝麻菜叶、樱桃番茄、牛油果，奶酪和黄油区，帕玛森奶酪。

sentences.en: Baking aisle, pine nuts, condiment aisle, olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
sentences.zh: 烘焙区，松子，调味品区，橄榄油和香醋。

sentences.en: And spice aisle, salt and pepper.
sentences.zh: 香料区，盐和胡椒。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I do want to say the last thing in this list is a note to you, Kevin, and your wife.
sentences.zh: 我确实想说，这个列表里的最后一项是给你的，凯文，还有你的妻子的一条便签。

sentences.en: Quote, I hope you and your wife enjoy the salad and have a wonderful Valentine's Day.
sentences.zh: 引述：我希望你和你的妻子喜欢这道沙拉，并度过一个美妙的情人节。

sentences.en: And then there's a heart, a moon.
sentences.zh: 然后是一个爱心，一个月亮。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's got those nice little touches too.
sentences.zh: 是的，它也有那些很好的小细节。

sentences.en: So this is one thing that Bing can do, but it can also do a lot of other things.
sentences.zh: 所以这是必应能做的一件事，但它也能做很多其他事情。

sentences.en: Here's another example.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个例子。

sentences.en: I've been thinking about getting an e-bike.
sentences.zh: 我一直在考虑买一辆电动自行车。

sentences.en: I'm not sure I'm going to get one yet, but I'm kind of curious about them.
sentences.zh: 我不确定现在是不是要买，但我对它们有点好奇。

sentences.en: And I'm looking for one that can fit into the back of my car.
sentences.zh: 我在找一辆能塞进我车后备箱的。

sentences.en: So I'm going to ask Bing, what are some top rated e-bikes and can they fit into the trunk of a Toyota Highlander?
sentences.zh: 所以我要问必应，有哪些评价很高的电动自行车，它们能塞进丰田汉兰达的后备箱吗？

sentences.en: So it's searching for top rated e-bikes.
sentences.zh: 所以它正在搜索评价很高的电动自行车。

sentences.en: Now it's searching for Toyota Highlander trunk dimensions.

sentences.zh: 那么作为人工智能搜索引擎的必应，难道不会侵蚀微软那巨大的收入来源吗？

sentences.zh: 这难道不会让微软和必应随着时间的推移盈利能力也变差吗？

sentences.en: Sure, but you have to remember, Microsoft is a tiny, tiny part of the search industry.
sentences.zh: 当然，但你必须记住，微软在搜索行业中只占极小极小的份额。

sentences.en: And Microsoft has a lot of other ways of making money.
sentences.zh: 而且微软有很多其他赚钱的途径。

sentences.en: So they are not nearly as dependent on search advertising revenue as Google is.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对搜索广告收入的依赖远没有谷歌那么大。

sentences.en: And so Microsoft sees this as basically all upside for them.
sentences.zh: 因此，微软认为这基本上全是对他们有利的。

sentences.en: Their CEO, Satya Nadella, said last week that for every 1% of market share that Bing takes from Google, they can make $2 billion more in advertising revenue.
sentences.zh: 他们的首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉上周表示，必应从谷歌那里每抢占1%的市场份额，他们就能多赚20亿美元的广告收入。

sentences.en: So for them, this chance to kind of eat away at Google's dominance in search is basically all upside.
sentences.zh: 所以对他们来说，这种蚕食谷歌在搜索领域主导地位的机会基本上全是利好。

sentences.en: They don't have a ton to lose.
sentences.zh: 他们没有什么好损失的。

sentences.en: They very much see this as an opportunity to hit Google right in the core of their business model.
sentences.zh: 他们非常将此视为一个直击谷歌商业模式核心的机会。

sentences.en: And if they can do that, if they can make Bing the household go-to search engine, then they are going to be able to set the terms for how to monetize it and eventually maybe earn
sentences.zh: 如果他们能做到这一点，如果他们能让必应成为家喻户晓的首选搜索引擎，那么他们就能制定如何将其变现的游戏规则，并最终可能赢回

sentences.en: back some of that advertising revenue that they're losing by switching to this new model.
sentences.zh: 因转向这种新模式而失去的部分广告收入。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: For example, it seems highly plausible that Bing's chatbot could be programmed to promote certain
sentences.zh: 例如，极其合乎逻辑的是，必应的聊天机器人可能会被编程，以推广某些

sentences.en: products above others and basically become very profitable as an advertising model.
sentences.zh: 产品优于其他产品，并基本上作为一种广告模式变得非常赚钱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There are tons of ways you could monetize this new AI chatbot search thing.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过无数种方式将这种新的人工智能聊天机器人搜索业务变现。

sentences.en: You could have it sort of subtly slip in references to certain products or you could just have
sentences.zh: 你可以让它巧妙地顺带提及某些产品，或者你也可以在人工智能搜索结果旁边

sentences.en: a little sort of sidebar on the AI search results that says, by the way, here are some sites where you can go buy this stuff that we've now told you about.
sentences.zh: 弄一个小小侧边栏，上面写着，顺便说一句，这里有一些网站，你可以去买我们刚才跟你说过这些东西。

sentences.en: If I'm Microsoft, it seems like there might be one flaw in this grand plan to kneecap Google and become supreme when it comes to search, which is that chat GPT, the technology that
sentences.zh: 如果我是微软，这个旨在暗算谷歌并在搜索领域称霸的宏伟计划似乎有一个缺陷，那就是ChatGPT，这项

sentences.en: now powers this new Bing, it makes a lot of mistakes, right?
sentences.zh: 现在赋能新必应的技术，会犯很多错误，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, Kevin, you talked to us about that in our first conversation about the technology.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，凯文，我们在关于这项技术的第一期对话中，你就跟我们谈过这个。

sentences.en: It makes math mistakes.
sentences.zh: 它会犯数学错误。

sentences.en: It makes factual mistakes.
sentences.zh: 它会犯事实错误。

sentences.en: And its leaders have actually acknowledged this to you in interviews that I know you've done.
sentences.zh: 而且它的高管实际上在你知道我做过的采访中向你承认过这一点。

sentences.en: So isn't that possibly a very big vulnerability for Microsoft?
sentences.zh: 所以这对微软来说难道不是一个非常大的潜在漏洞吗？

sentences.en: Because the one thing we want our searches to be above all is accurate.
sentences.zh: 因为我们希望搜索结果首先做到的就是准确。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is a real issue.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实是个问题。

sentences.en: And I would say the main issue that is underlying this entire trend in using AI for search.
sentences.zh: 而且我想说，这是整个利用人工智能进行搜索的趋势背后最核心的问题。

sentences.en: These large language models are very good at generating sort of clean, plausible sounding sentences by predicting the next word in the sentence over and over again.
sentences.zh: 这些大语言模型非常擅长通过一遍又一遍地预测句子中的下一个词，来生成那种干净、听起来貌似合理的句子。

sentences.en: But that is a very different thing from looking up factual information.
sentences.zh: 但这与查阅事实信息是完全不同的两回事。

sentences.en: And actually, a few days after the Bing relaunch, people started pointing out that it was making all kinds of mistakes, too.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在必应重新发布几天后，人们就开始指出它也在犯各种各样的错误。

sentences.en: It was just making stuff up.
sentences.zh: 它完全是在胡编乱造。

sentences.en: It got some numbers wrong.
sentences.zh: 它弄错了一些数字。

sentences.en: And you can see this.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以看出来。

sentences.en: I mean, when I was testing the new Bing last week, I was looking for something to do with my family over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 我是说，上周我测试新必应的时候，我在找周末能和家人一起做的事情。

sentences.en: And so I said, you know, what are some kid-friendly activities that I could do in my hometown this weekend?
sentences.zh: 于是我说，你知道的，这个周末我在家乡有什么适合小孩参加的活动吗？

sentences.en: And it generated a list of options.
sentences.zh: 然后它生成了一个选项列表。

sentences.en: And of the three things that it listed me, all of them had already happened.
sentences.zh: 在它列出的三个事项中，所有这些活动其实都已经结束了。

sentences.en: One of them happened the previous weekend.
sentences.zh: 其中一个发生在头上个周末。

sentences.en: One of them happened two weekends earlier.
sentences.zh: 另一个发生在两周前的周末。

sentences.en: One of them was a Hanukkah party that happened in mid-December.
sentences.zh: 还有一个是月中举办的光明节派对。

sentences.en: So none of them were actually things that I could do that coming weekend.
sentences.zh: 所以没有一个是接下来的那个周末我真正能去参加的活动。

sentences.en: Which basically makes that an entirely useless search.
sentences.zh: 这就基本上让这次搜索变得毫无用处。

sentences.en: Entirely useless search, but one that sounded very plausible.
sentences.zh: 完全毫无用处的搜索，但它听起来却非常合情合理。

sentences.en: And if I hadn't gone to the underlying websites and actually looked at the dates, I would have had no idea.
sentences.zh: 如果我没有去查阅底层的网站并实际核对日期，我根本不会发现。

sentences.en: And I might have shown up expecting a Hanukkah party or a Lunar New Year party that had already happened and looked like a real idiot.
sentences.zh: 我可能就会满怀期待地跑过去，结果却发现光明节派对或农历新年派对早就已经结束了，看起来就像个十足的笨蛋。

sentences.en: So that's a benign example, relatively.
sentences.zh: 所以相对来说，这是一个无伤大雅的例子。

sentences.en: But you can imagine this going way worse.
sentences.zh: 但你可以想象事情会变得多糟。

sentences.en: People ask search engines for very important questions.
sentences.zh: 人们会向搜索引擎提出非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: Questions about how to save and spend their money.
sentences.zh: 关于如何储蓄和花钱的问题。

sentences.en: Questions about medications and medical advice.
sentences.zh: 关于药物和医疗建议的问题。

sentences.en: People really do put a lot of trust in their search engines.
sentences.zh: 人们确实对他们的搜索引擎寄予了极大的信任。

sentences.en: And if these search engines are just generating plausible-sounding but wrong answers, that could be a very big problem.
sentences.zh: 如果这些搜索引擎只是在生成听起来合理但实际上错误的答案，那可能会成为一个非常严重的问题。

sentences.en: Well, Kevin, given how important this is, does Microsoft have a plan to make AI being more factual?
sentences.zh: 那么，凯文，鉴于这如此重要，微软有什么计划让AI必应变得更符合事实吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they do.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们有。

sentences.en: They say that this model will improve over time as they see, you know, the kinds of mistakes that it makes and they change the underlying technology and they make it more reliable.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，随着他们发现这种模型所犯的各种错误，并对底层技术进行修改以使其更可靠，这个模型会随着时间推移不断改进。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's one camp of people who says, yeah, that sounds right because
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有一派人认为，是的，听起来确实如此，因为

sentences.en: things on the internet, you know, some of them tend to get more reliable over time.
sentences.zh: 互联网上的事物，你知道的，随着时间的推移往往会变得更加可靠。

sentences.en: Like, I've been thinking about when Wikipedia first came out.
sentences.zh: 就像，我一直在回想维基百科刚问世的时候。

sentences.en: It was seen as very unreliable.
sentences.zh: 它当时被认为非常不可靠。

sentences.en: Like, your teachers and your parents, they would say, like, don't trust anything you read.
sentences.zh: 就像，你的老师和父母会告诉你，不要相信你读到的任何东西。

sentences.en: Don't trust Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 不要相信维基百科。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That was drilled into us as kids.
sentences.zh: 我们从小就被灌输这种观念。

sentences.en: And then, over time, as Wikipedia got better and more popular and developed these kind of internal standards, it got more trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 然后，随着时间推移，维基百科变得更好、更受欢迎，并发展出了这种内部标准，它就变得更值得信赖了。

sentences.en: And we also sort of developed a sense as consumers of what kinds of things on Wikipedia were more trustworthy than others.
sentences.zh: 而且作为消费者，我们也逐渐培养出一种直觉，知道维基百科上的哪些内容比其他内容更值得信赖。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's another camp of people who say, actually, no, that's not what's happening here.
sentences.zh: 还有另一派人认为，其实不然，这里发生的情况并非如此。

sentences.en: This is not just another kind of self-improving product because these AI models, these large language models, are fundamentally untrustworthy.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是又一种自我改进的产品，因为这些人工智能模型，这些大语言模型，从根本上就是不可信的。

sentences.en: They don't have a way of distinguishing between true and false information.
sentences.zh: 它们没有办法区分真实信息和虚假信息。

sentences.en: All they are designed to do is to predict the next words in a sequence.
sentences.zh: 它们被设计的唯一目的就是预测序列中的下一个词。

sentences.en: And that kind of technology can never become trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 这种技术永远不可能变得值得信赖。

sentences.en: So, at the end of the day, Kevin, what you're really saying here is that this basic ritual in our lives is undergoing a revolution, how we search.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，凯文，你在这里真正想说的是，我们生活中这个基本的日常习惯正在经历一场革命，也就是我们搜索的方式。

sentences.en: And I now admit this is an episode.
sentences.zh: 我现在承认这是一个大事件。

sentences.en: This does seem like a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这确实感觉像是一件大事。

sentences.en: And my really big question as we conclude the conversation is, do I now need to download
sentences.zh: 在我们结束对话之际，我最想问的一个大问题是，我现在需要下载

sentences.en: Bing?
sentences.zh: 必应吗？

sentences.en: Because I'm a Google user in a Google-using household who works for a Google product-using company.
sentences.zh: 因为我是一个谷歌用户，生活在一个使用谷歌的家庭里，还在一家使用谷歌产品的公司工作。

sentences.en: So, that would be a big change.
sentences.zh: 所以，那将会是一个巨大的改变。

sentences.en: Well, I'm not going to tell you how to live your life.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我不会教你该怎么生活。

sentences.en: Use whatever search engine you feel most comfortable with.
sentences.zh: 用你觉得最顺手的搜索引擎就行。

sentences.en: I have started using Bing mostly to test it because I cover this stuff and I find it very interesting and sometimes very helpful.
sentences.zh: 我开始使用必应主要是为了测试它，因为我负责报道这方面的领域，我发现它非常有趣，有时也非常有用。

sentences.en: But I would say that no matter which search engine you use, the larger point here is that this is all happening so faSt.
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是，无论你用哪个搜索引擎，这里更重要的一点是，这一切发生得太快了。

sentences.en: I've been covering tech for a long time and I have never seen a new technology work its way into the heart of the tech industry so quickly.
sentences.zh: 我报道科技已经很久了，从未见过一种新技术能如此迅速地渗入到科技产业的核心。

sentences.en: I mean, it was just a couple weeks ago, really, that we were talking about ChatGPT, this new and sort of weird and interesting chatbot.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的就在几周前，我们还在讨论ChatGPT这个新奇、古怪又有趣的聊天机器人。

sentences.en: And now the same technology is being put into products that billions of people use every day.
sentences.zh: 而现在，同样的技术正被应用到数十亿人每天都在使用的产品中。

sentences.en: It happened so, so quickly.
sentences.zh: 这一切发生得太快太快了。

sentences.en: So, I have never seen a moment like this where it felt like something so fundamental to the way the internet works, the way that society works really, is being upended so rapidly.
sentences.zh: 所以，我从未见过这样的时刻，感觉互联网运作方式乃至社会运作方式中如此根本的东西，正在以如此迅猛的速度被颠覆。

sentences.en: Well, Kevin, as always, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，凯文，一如既往，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.zh: 情人节快乐。

sentences.zh: 也祝你情人节快乐。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎进了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场残酷、混乱且有时扣人心弦的权力争斗中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《都市》（Metro）的最新一期中，由我萨拉·科尼格（Sarah Koenig）为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.zh: 欢迎在各大播客平台收听。
